frames.metadata: {"channel_offset":17,"evidence":"live device readback, 2026-09-01","magic":"0x70","magic_offset":0,"notes":"Field positions come from Antelope's own report format: every write carries header report_id 0x70 with ext2 and ext3 zero, and a field list whose first entry is the target id and whose second is the value - set_pre_gain is [id ubyte, gain byte], set_pre_phantom is [id ubyte, phantom ubyte]. That gives 16/17/18. opcode is left null because the byte at offset 4 is a LENGTH, 16 + payload, not an opcode: PROTOCOL.md 4a labels @4 on the request 0x10 'sub-command, constant' while the response layout in the same block carries 0x0140 there, and 16 + 0 = 0x10 while 16 + 304 = 0x0140. A 3-byte payload gives 0x13, which is the value captures show for SET_PARAM. WHAT IS NOT HERE: the selector byte at offset 16. The format's payload_id is an index in Antelope's request table, space 0-41, not that byte - captured command frames in this family carry 0x50, 0xa2, 0xd3, 0xd4 there. Do not populate params[].id from payload_id. Naming: 4a's (category, index) at @8/@12 are the fields the format calls ext2 and ext3.","opcode":null,"opcode_name":null,"opcode_offset":4,"param_id_offset":16,"status":"derived","value_offset":18}

transport.notes: Identical to Orion Studio III on every field, so the transport layer really is shared across the family. One difference that matters for transport.py: the HID report descriptor contains no Report ID item, so on Linux hidraw a write must be 321 bytes -- a leading 0x00 report-number byte plus the 320-byte payload. Worth dumping /sys/class/hidraw/hidrawN/device/report_descriptor on an Orion to see whether the same applies there. Full descriptor for this device: 06 a0 ff 09 01 a1 01 09 02 a1 00 06 a1 ff 09 03 09 04 15 80 25 7f 35 00 45 ff 75 08 96 40 01 81 02 09 05 09 06 15 80 25 7f 35 00 45 ff 75 08 96 40 01 91 02 c0 c0

constraints.metadata: "0x01 / 0x02 = crash / unknown-dangerous (BusFault family) -- a hardware-safety block, unrelated to AFX. 0x1a / 0x1c / 0x23 added 2026-09-03 as a PRECAUTION before any AFX / Synergy Core LICENSED-plugin-chain work -- see SCOPE.md §4. This is a policy about Antelope's purchasable, activation-gated plugin catalogue (Auto-Tune, amp sims, specialized EQ/comp, etc.), NOT a stance against using the device's DSP unit in general: AuraVerb (0x1d) and the surround per-speaker EQ (readback category 0x1a, unrelated write-opcode collision) are both bundled, non-activated features and are fully decoded + in scope. Since 2026-09-04, from two macOS Launcher captures: 0x23 / param 0xd7 = the AFX SLOT-ASSIGN frame (put plugin instance <handle> on channel <ch>, or 0x00 to clear) -- see frame.afx_slot. Placing/clearing a plugin is bucket E (instantiate/load/remove), so 0x23 STAYS forbidden and build_* must never emit it; frame.afx_slot documents it for observation + readback decoding only. 0x1c / param 0xd5 = the plugin PARAMETER stream -- bucket D, frame-counted but never decoded, stays forbidden. 0x1a as a WRITE OPCODE has never been observed on this device at all -- it is blocked purely as a blanket cross-device precaution, carried over from the Zen Go profile (zen_go_sc.json), where 0x1a and 0x1c share param 0xd5 in one undecoded capture (capture_07_dsp) and 0x1a is actually a *candidate for the Zen Go's mic-modeling/emuMic frame* -- an in-scope, non-AFX feature -- not a confirmed licensed-plugin opcode. So on this device 0x1a stays forbidden as 'unconfirmed, blocked until proven safe,' not because it is known AFX/DSP content. The per-slot BYPASS toggle is a different frame (opcode 0x14 / param 0x98, bucket B, frame.afx_slot.bypass) and is NOT forbidden -- but ships no builder yet (needs a handle from the 0x0c/0x15 readback, undecoded). build_* refuses a forbidden opcode."

The front-panel/Launcher EMU button shows on a channel only in Mic mode (absent in Line/Hi-Z) -- earlier work saw '7-12' because the reference unit had preamps 5-6 in Line. FULLY CONFIRMED 2026-09-03 by a live usbmon capture of the webUI driving EMU on preamp 5/6 (captures/new/webui-emumic-preamp56-2026-09-03.frames.txt): the 0xe5 frame carries [18]=0x00 for preamp 5 and [18]=0x01 for preamp 6 -- the channel_bias -4 mapping holds to the bottom of the range, directly observed on the wire (was extrapolation). The pair is link pair 2 (SET_LINK 0x14 a2 00 02 seen on disable), and the phantom/gain sync commands (SET_PARAM 0x51 / 0x50) address the pair as channel index 4 & 5.","enabled_offset":19,"magic":"0x70","magic_offset":0,"model_offset":20,"notes":"MIC MODELING / 'emuMic' -- the front-panel EMU button on preamps 5-12 (8 channels), shown per channel only in Mic mode. Runs Antelope's mic-emulation DSP (for their Edge Solo / Edge Duo / Edge Note modelling mics + model packs). Opcode 0x17 is SHARED: param_id at [16] disambiguates -- 0xd4 = virtual mixer (frame.mix_command), 0xe5 = mic modeling. Frame `e5 05 <ch> <en> <model> <swap> <pattern>`, bytes 16-22, rest 0. [17]=0x05 const; [18]=channel = 0-based input channel index - 4 (preamp 7 -> 2 ... preamp 12 -> 7); [19]=modeling ENABLED (1/0); [20]=MODEL ID (0 = EdgeDuo / raw mic, no emulation -- the default; 1..N = the emulation models, see profiles/mic_models.json); [21]=CHANNEL-ORDER SWAP (0/1); [22]=POLAR PATTERN, always a 0-based INDEX (NOT a class code -- corrected 2026-09-01 from macos-emumic-polar-patterns). With model 0 (EdgeDuo raw) it is the free 0-100 continuous morph (0 omni / 50 cardioid / 100 figure-8), user-confirmed. With an emulation model selected it is a small integer index into that model's pattern list, and its range is per-model: fixed mics lock it at 0 (models 2,5,6,8,13,14,15,17 -- one pattern); models 3,4,7 sweep 0..2 (omni/cardioid/fig-8); models 9,10,11 sweep 0..8 (9-detent multipattern); models 1,12,16,18 only 0..1 were swept (a 3rd value may exist -- not confirmed). Selecting a model writes [22] = that model's DEFAULT pattern index (0 for fixed, 1 = cardioid for the 3-way mics, 4 = cardioid for the 9-way mics) -- this is the value earlier misrecorded as 'pattern_class' in mic_models.json. Enable/pattern(model 0)/swap decoded 2026-08-31 from macos-ch7-8-micmodeling-* / macos-ch9-10_11-12-micmodeling-*; model IDs from 'emumic-model-select-...' (Windows KVM, 18 models cycled on preamps 7-8); per-model pattern-index ranges from macos-emumic-polar-patterns (2026-09-01, all 19 models swept on preamps 7-8). Whole state every frame; params MIRROR across the linked preamp pair (Launcher sends [18]=N then [18]=N+1). Disabling sets [19]=[21]=[22]=0. SIDE EFFECTS of enabling: the Launcher also turns on 48V phantom for the pair (SET_PARAM param 0x51) and links the preamp pair (SET_LINK space 0). No readback CATEGORY identified in the 0x74/0x75 protocol (cat 0x1a turned out to be the surround per-speaker EQ, cat 0x07 is unresolved EQ/filter data -- neither is mic modeling); in the passive 0x73 stream only the phantom bit (0x10) moves. build_micmodeling_command(profile, channel, enabled, pattern, swap, model); not in cli.py.","opcode":"0x17","opcode_name":"SET_MIC_MODELING","opcode_offset":4,"param_id":"0xe5","param_id_offset":16,"pattern_offset":22,"pattern_range":[0,100],"pattern_range_note":"[0,100] is the model-0 (EdgeDuo raw) continuous morph range. See notes and mic_models.json.","subcmd":"0x05","subcmd_offset":17,"swap_offset":21}

{"adat_gain_base_offset":75,"bus_block":{"base_offset":28,"bytes_per_bus":3,"level_byte_offset":0,"notes":"Same 'parallel array, N bytes per slot' idea as gain_base_offset/status_base_offset above, but for output buses instead of input channels: byte offset for bus N = base_offset + bytes_per_bus*N + field_offset. Confirmed for ALL 6 bus ids: 0/1/2/5 via captures mona/hp1/hp2/monb (2026-08, level ramps + dim/mute/mono toggles), and 3/4 (line/reamp) via capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08, level ramps at offsets 37 and 40 + a mute toggle on bus 3). Every SET_PARAM command in each log matched the very next state_report reading at this formula's offset. reserved_byte_offset (+2) never changed in any capture; true padding, or just never exercised, is unconfirmed. dim/mono were never exercised on buses 3/4 and may not apply to a line/reamp output. NOTE: the status byte's mute bit (0x04) also reads 1 whenever that bus is at level 96 with no mute command -- see params.bus_mute.","reserved_byte_offset":2,"status_bits":{"dim":{"mask":"0x08","shift":3},"mono":{"mask":"0x10","shift":4},"mute":{"mask":"0x04","shift":2}},"status_byte_offset":1},"channel_meter_base_offset":157,"channel_meter_notes":"RESOLVED 2026-09-05 (step 4, see the antelope-ctl-UI-test sandbox's webui/METERS.md 'step 4' entry (not in this repo)) -- this is NOT a per-preamp-channel block at all, and never was. Bytes 157/158/159/160 are the four VIRTUAL MIXER buses' own master meters (byte N = Mix (N-157+1) master), not one byte per physical preamp. The 2026-09-01 recapture (feeding preamps 1-4, seeing 157-160 move) only looked like a per-channel preamp meter because each mix bus's DEFAULT strip patching happens to include the matching preamp among its many sources (Mix 1 strip 1 defaults from surround 1 <- surround_in ch1 <- preamp 1; Mix 2's 32 default strips include preamp 1-8 at slots 16-23; etc) -- three hops of coincidence, not a direct tap. This is consistent with every earlier finding here: the surround_in correlation (Mix 1 draws from the surround bus's output by default), the mix_ch1-lights-157 test, and com_rec-does-nothing (com_rec isn't a mix bus). Bytes 161-168 (the rest of the nominal 12-byte span) were NEVER confirmed to move in an exhaustive full-320-byte scan of FIVE capture files -- there are only 4 mixers, not 12 channels, so there was never really a 12-byte per-channel block; 157-160 is the real signal, 161-168 is unexplained padding/unrelated. The webui's preamp meter strips (webui/static/index.html applyMeters -> .pre[data-ch] [data-meter]) have been reading this Mix-master block and displaying it as if it were per-preamp input the whole time -- this went unnoticed because Mix 1-4 default to being fed by the matching preamps, so it LOOKED right until routing was repatched away from that default (the original bug report this whole investigation started from). The TRUE physical-preamp meter was searched for exhaustively (both 0x73 and 0x75 report types, every byte, five capture files) and not found anywhere in the HID control stream -- this is a USB Audio Class device, and the real per-input meters the Launcher's Preamp tab shows are most likely computed host-side from the live PCM audio stream over the isochronous audio endpoint, a completely different mechanism this project has not captured or analyzed. Older passes below, kept for the reasoning trail (steps 1-3, all superseded by this reframing): STATUS 2026-09-05 (step 3, see the sandbox's webui/METERS.md 'step 3' entry): this block's identity is LESS certain than the step-2 pass below implies -- a Windows Launcher cross-check showed the real Preamp tab meters stay silent under a routing setup that lit this block up, and a separate, cleaner candidate (bytes 177/178, see channel_meter_base_offset's own notes) looks like the real Mix 1 master meter instead. This 157+ch block is NOT confirmed to be, and increasingly looks like it is NOT, a physical preamp-input meter -- it may be the Surround tab's meters or something else. Physical preamps and virtual mixers are two distinct concepts (per the user) and must not be conflated here. The TRUE preamp meter the Launcher's Preamp tab reads is still unidentified -- see METERS.md 'genuinely unresolved' for what a decisive test would need. Older passes below, kept for the reasoning trail: CORRECTED 2026-09-05 (step 2), full writeup + byte-level evidence in the sandbox webui/METERS.md (not in this repo) -- this is NOT a fixed per-channel analog-input tap, and NOT a fixed per-`surround_in`-channel tap either (an earlier pass at this note claimed the latter; disproven by a follow-up test). DECISIVE TEST: with a live mic signal on preamp 2 already showing at byte 158 (via surround_in ch2, which preamp 2 was routed into), routing that SAME preamp-2 signal into a SECOND destination (mix_ch1 routing-dest strip 1, dest id 10, channel 0) made byte **157** light up to match it too -- even though surround_in ch1 had nothing routed into it and stayed untouched throughout. So 157 is not 'surround_in channel 1' specifically: it is a slot in a small SHARED POOL that gets dynamically claimed by whichever internal signal path(s) currently carry audio, drawn from across multiple distinct buses (confirmed in: surround_in, mix_ch strips; confirmed NOT in: com_rec -- routing the same live preamp signal into a com_rec channel produced no change anywhere in the block; mix_ch2-4/afx_in/ADAT/S-PDIF untested) -- not a fixed identity per byte. It shows correct preamp levels only when surround_in happens to be routed straight-through from the matching preamp AND nothing else in the pool's scope is competing for that slot -- both true by default, which is why this looked like a clean per-preamp meter for so long. The exact allocation rule (which bus(es) feed the pool, order/priority when multiple signals compete for the same slot count) is UNRESOLVED -- every test so far has had at most 2 simultaneous active signals; a live-capture-based investigation (see PROTOCOL.md methodology) is more likely to resolve this than further black-box polling, which already produced several since-retracted false leads during this same investigation (see the sandbox's webui/METERS.md). Three identical mirror copies of the whole 12-byte pool still exist at bases 157, 169 and 221 -- use 157. This supersedes meter_report.channel_meter_base_offset (0x75 @32), which on this unit is NOT per-channel: only its byte 32 is live (a monitor/summed level) and byte 33 is a 0/1 flag that the old 32+channel formula misreads as channel 1 pinned at clip.","channel_meter_scale":"inverted: 0x60 (96) at rest/silence, falls toward 0x00 as level rises. See params.sample_rate.","offset":18},"screen_brightness_byte_offset":{"notes":"The device's front-panel screen brightness, 0-100 (0x00-0x64), one plain byte. NOTE opcode 0x17 is SHARED: param_id 0xe5 on the same opcode is mic modeling (frame.micmodeling_command) -- always check [16]. One frame per (mix, channel) strip, carrying that strip's WHOLE state every time. CONFIRMED from macos-mix1-send-pan-fader-mute-solo-link (2026-08, native macOS): [16]=0xd4 [17]=0x05 constant; [18]=mix number 0-3 (0 = Mix 1 .. 3 = Mix 4) -- CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 via the cat-0x04 readback, which returns an independent record for each of the four indices (the original capture had only ever shown mix 0); [19]=channel **0-32**: 1-32 = the input strips (each mix has 32 -- the user's solo click re-sent all 32, a handy channel-count probe) and **0 = the MIX MASTER strip** (CONFIRMED 2026-09-01 from captures/new/mix1-masterfaderplay.pcapng: sweeping the Mix 1 master fader emits 68 frames, all `d4 05 00 00 <fader> 20 60` -- channel 0, pan/send held constant. The Launcher writes channel 0 itself, so it is a normal target); [20]=FADER, raw = attenuation in -dB, 0 = 0dB/unity .. 90 = -90dB (matches the UI's 0..-90 range); [21]=PAN + FLAGS -- low 6 bits (pan_mask) = pan, pan_center 0x20, so 0x02 = full-left (-30), 0x20 = center, 0x3e = full-right (+30) i.e. raw = 32 + degrees; bit 0x40 = MUTE; bit 0x80 = SOLO; [22]=SEND level, 0-96 (0x60 = 0dB, 0 = -inf; same 0-96 scale as bus_level). No target byte past 22. READBACK: frame.readback category 0x04, index = mix number 0..3 -- FULLY DECODED + hardware round-trip verified 2026-08-31. The record is 33 three-byte slots in this frame's own field order (fader, pan|flags, send); slot N is exactly the strip written as `channel` N -- including slot 0 = channel 0 = the mix master -- so the readback and the write frame share a layout the way routing does, with no special case at either end. That round trip also confirmed [18] really is the mix number (all four mixes return their own record) and that [22] is stored send state, not a meter. protocol.parse_mixer_record; CLI `mix-status`. Also category 0x1b = the SURROUND GLOBAL readback, not a mixer table (corrected 2026-09-04 -- see frame.readback.categories.0x1b); mixer BUS levels are in the 0x73 state report's bus_block (offsets 28-45), not in any readback category. CLI: `mix-set <mix> <ch|master> [--fader dB] [--pan] [--send] [--mute] [--solo]`, which read-modify-writes the strip via the cat-0x04 readback (this frame carries the WHOLE strip, so a partial write would reset the untouched fields) and verifies afterwards. hazards.metadata: {"effect_on_discrete_8_pro":"opcodes 0x01 and 0x02 wedged the USB controller -- every further write ETIMEDOUT, the device dropped off the bus ('device descriptor read/64, error -71'), and NEITHER a driver rebind NOR the kernel port power-cycle recovered it. Only unplugging the unit's power did.","enforced_by":"constraints.forbidden_opcodes + constraints.allowed_opcodes","notes":"Which of 0x01/0x02 is responsible was not isolated; both forbidden. An unmapped opcode could in principle reach a routine that writes non-volatile memory or enters recalibration -- nothing observed suggests that happened, nothing rules it out. This asymmetry is the whole argument against blind sweeps, including on Orion.","rule":"only send opcodes from constraints.allowed_opcodes; never a value from user input; rate-limit writes (constraints.min_write_interval_ms)"}
hazards.name: blind_opcode_sweeps
hazards.notes: Which of 0x01/0x02 is responsible was not isolated; both forbidden. An unmapped opcode could in principle reach a routine that writes non-volatile memory or enters recalibration -- nothing observed suggests that happened, nothing rules it out. This asymmetry is the whole argument against blind sweeps, including on Orion.
hazards.rule: only send opcodes from constraints.allowed_opcodes; never a value from user input; rate-limit writes (constraints.min_write_interval_ms)

hazards.name: channel_index_out_of_range
hazards.notes: Orion's CLI currently only warns past channels.confirmed_indices and sends anyway. Given the sibling behaviour that is too loose -- an out-of-range write should be refused unless --force. The same byte carries bus ids for bus params, where 0-5 are legal, so a single global channel-count check is wrong.
hazards.rule: bound-check the channel index against the RIGHT address space before writing -- constraints.channel_bounds (0-11) for gain/mode/phantom/phase, constraints.adat_channel_bounds (0-15) for adat_gain, constraints.bus_ids for bus params. Refuse, don't clamp-and-hope.

hazards.name: foreign_enum_values
hazards.notes: Orion does have input_mode 3 = direct (confirmed here), so this specific value is fine ON ORION -- the hazard is the general one: a shared profile format must not let one device's enum leak into another's code path.
hazards.rule: validate every enum value against THIS profile; never pass one through from another device's profile or straight from user input

identity.name: Antelope Orion Studio Synergy Core
identity.notes: Composite USB device; control is entirely via the vendor HID interface (iface 3). UAC2 audio-control interface has no Feature Units. Model lineage (for disambiguation): this is the 2020 'Orion Studio Synergy Core' -- the third Orion Studio generation, after the 2015 Orion Studio and the 2017 Orion Studio Rev.2017. Not the same as the Orion 32 / Orion 32+ / Orion HD (the multichannel converters). The device reports its own name as 'OrionStudio_III' in readback category 0x01, hence the file's old name orion_studio_3.json (renamed to orion_studio_sc.json 2026-09-03, matching the *_sc.json Synergy Core family naming -- zen_go_sc, discrete_8_pro_sc, discrete_4_sc, discrete_4_pro_sc).

params.metadata: {"applies_to":"buses","evidence":"captures mona/monb/hp1/hp2 (2026-08): Mute button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches status bit 'mute' (0x04). Also confirmed on bus 3 in capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08) via the settings-tab Line-output mute toggle. Not tested on buses 4 or 5.","id":"0x48","notes":"The status byte's 0x04 bit is ALSO set, with no SET_PARAM(0x48) command, whenever a bus sits at bus_level == 96 (max). First seen once on bus 0 (mona capture) and thought to be a fluke; now REPRODUCED deliberately in settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08) on BOTH bus 3 and bus 4 -- the bit switches on exactly as the level sweep reaches 0x60 and switches off again on the very next step below max, every time. So bit 0x04 in the readback means 'muted OR at maximum level' and cannot distinguish the two on its own. Any bus-status readback must check bus_level: if level==96, treat 0x04 as 'at max' and report mute state as unknown/false unless a mute was explicitly sent. See unresolved_state_offsets.","status":"confirmed","type":"bool"}

params.metadata: {"evidence":"capture chlink (2026-08): all 6 pairs (index 0-5) toggled on then off in turn; frame.link_command.pair_index_offset and .enabled_offset were read directly off the wire for all 12 commands (6 on, 6 off) and matched the test sequence exactly","frame":"frame.link_command (a distinct shape from every other param in this file -- NOT SET_PARAM)","live_sync_while_linked":"CONFIRMED (capture ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test, 2026-08): while a pair is linked, changing gain, phantom, OR phase_invert on either channel is mirrored to the other channel on essentially every command -- gain_base_offset bytes for both channels moved in lockstep through a full ramp (offsets 49 and 50 tracking together, ~8ms apart), and status_base_offset bytes for both channels flipped together for both the phantom bit (0x10) and the phase_invert bit (0x40). CORRECTED 2026-08: re-examining the same ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test.tsv capture that established this shows the outgoing 0x70/0x13 frames directly -- every gain change during the linked sweep produced TWO separate outgoing SET_PARAM(gain=0x50, channel, value) frames (channel 0 then channel 1, ~2ms apart, same value), not one command with an observed two-channel effect. So \"mirrored to the other channel\" here means the Launcher software issued two commands, one per channel -- not that the device propagates a single write. Same conclusion as side_effects above: this is an application-layer behavior that any alternative controller (including this repo's cli.py) must replicate itself if it wants the same result; the device does not do it for you. STRONGEST CONFIRMATION (user, 2026-08): turning the PHYSICAL front-panel gain wheel on a linked channel moves ONLY that channel -- the linked partner does not follow. The hardware wheel bypasses all host software on the input path, so this proves the device firmware has zero link-propagation logic; and the Launcher evidently only mirrors changes it initiates from its own UI, not hardware-wheel changes.","mode_requires_unlink":"CONFIRMED (same capture, matches user report): input_mode cannot be changed on a linked pair -- the Launcher grays out the control. The captured workflow was unlink -> change input_mode independently per channel (status_base_offset mode bits for ch1 and ch2 changed at separate, unsynced moments, each also resetting that channel's gain to a value appropriate for the new mode's range) -> re-link. Once re-linked, subsequent phase_invert/phantom/gain changes resumed syncing across both channels immediately (no extra step needed for those three). This is expected device behavior, not a bug in the CLI or a broken link.","notes":"No 'link enabled' bit has been found yet anywhere in the 0x73 state report -- every state_report byte that changed during this capture is already fully explained by the ordinary gain_base_offset/status_base_offset formula (as a side effect, see above), not a dedicated link flag. Whether link status can be READ BACK from the device at all is unknown; the Launcher UI may just track it client-side from what it has sent. Needs a dedicated whole-report diff (link on vs off, nothing else touched) before concluding there's no readback. Independently re-verified 2026-08 directly from the raw all_reports_ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test.tsv (9362 reports): only magics 0x70/0x73/0x75 appear anywhere in the file (no hidden fourth report type), the capture's 4 link/unlink commands are all pair_index=0x00 (pair 0, ch1&ch2) alternating enabled 1/0/1/0, and diffing the 0x73 state report immediately-before vs immediately-after each of those 4 commands yields zero changed bytes every time -- actively reconfirms \"no readback bit\", not just \"none found yet\", for this capture's toggles. ITEM CLOSED 2026-09-03 -- the dedicated whole-report diff was finally done against the LIVE device: raw 0x14 link toggle on preamp pair 3 (no gain/mode sync), 0x73 read 3x keeping only bytes stable across all reads, before vs after, for BOTH on and off, plus a re-read of readback cats 0x0c / 0x15 / 0x06. Zero stable bytes moved anywhere; the readback tables were byte-identical. So: the device DOES store link state (the front panel shows it, per side_effects) but exposes it nowhere over USB HID -- not in 0x73, not in any 0x74/0x75 readback category. A controller must track link state client-side (this CLI and the Launcher both do).","pairing":"see channels.link_pairs -- pair_index = channel_index // 2","side_effects":"Engaging a pair's link immediately triggered fresh SET_PARAM(input_mode) and/or SET_PARAM(gain) commands for the SECOND (higher-numbered) channel of that pair -- consistent with the device syncing that channel's mode/gain to the first channel's current settings. 'Room Correction OFF' = bypass the surround EQ for that speaker (the per-speaker EQ bypass -- surround_monitor.field_map.25_26 mask; user-confirmed there is no dedicated RC toggle). The 3 RC types (short / longer / longest -- more sweeps, more precision) differ only in the MEASUREMENT, and in a 2.0 setup ALL of them write the SAME correction to L and R (user tested both the short and the advanced mode 2026-09-03 -- L and R EQ came out identical each time). The 0.6 ms floor is a fixed processing latency the UI adds on top.","21_22":"per-speaker LEVEL, LE16. base 600 (0x0258) = 0 dB; 0.1 dB/step; range 0 = -60 dB .. 760 = +16 dB (USER-CONFIRMED 2026-09-03). **bit 7 of [22] = phase INVERT** (level tops at 760 = 0x02F8 so [22] bit 7 is free: 0x02 -> 0x82 on the invert toggle).","23_onward":"SIXTEEN parametric EQ bands, FULLY DECODED 2026-09-03 (srrnd-EQ-Q-and-mode + srrnd-EQ-L/R-* + srrnd-EQ-L-gain). One `0x87` frame carries all 16; the Launcher shows them as 2 pages of 8. **7-byte stride, band N at [23 + 7*N] (N 0..15): `<freq LE16 Hz> <Q LE16> <gain LE16 signed> <mode byte>`.** FREQ = literal Hz, 20 .. 20000 Hz per band (user). Q = LE16, value = Q x100, range 10 (Q 0.10) .. 1800 (Q 18.0), default 0x0047 = 71 = Q 0.71 (Butterworth) -- the byte I earlier called a `0x47` marker IS the Q low byte. GAIN = LE16 signed, 0.01 dB, -2400 (-24 dB) .. +1200 (+12 dB) (user). MODE byte: `0x02` = bell (bands 2-15, always). **Bands 1 and 16 are the end-band slots** (band 1 = low end, band 16 = high end), each with TWO user modes: SHELVING and BAND-PASS (Antelope's labels; a 'flat' line in the UI is just shelf/pass at 0 gain and is NOT a separate mode). **Observed mode-byte values** -- band 1: `0x00` (rest) toggling to `0x04` (srrnd-EQ-Q-and-mode, L); band 16: `0x00` (rest) toggling `0x01` <-> `0x03` (srrnd-LFE, on the LFE strip). So the encoding is NOT a clean bitfield -- band 1 uses {0x00, 0x04}, band 16 uses {0x01, 0x03} (plus 0x00 as the untouched default). Which of the two is 'shelving' vs 'band-pass' is not yet pinned -- ask the user, they toggled it. In BOTH modes gain works and Q sets the slope. On the CENTRE channel the end bands are bell (`0x02`) only. Default freqs per page 30/120/500/1400/3000/5500/9500/14000 Hz."},"frame":"opcode 0x87 @4, param_id 0xea @16, [17]=0x75 const, [18]=speaker 0..15, then the strip. LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: with a 2.0 Room Correction curve loaded, cat 0x1a idx 0 and idx 1 both carried that curve (identical L/R, as RC does), other indices were flat defaults. So this frame IS readable -- only the delay/level/invert head of the strip is not visible in cat 0x1a (bands only). Parsed + wired 2026-09-04: protocol.parse_surround_speaker_eq_record, CLI `surround-eq`. (The GLOBAL 0xab frame's readback is a separate category, 0x1b -- see params.surround_monitor.)

params.metadata: {"evidence":"macos-ch7-8 / -ch9-10_11-12: e5 05 <ch> <en> 00 <swap> <pattern>, pattern swept 0x00-0x64 step 4. emumic-model-select-tokyo800t-...-b47TU (18 models): e5 05 02 01 <model 0x01..0x12> 00 <default>, default in {0,1,4}; [19]=1 [21]=0 throughout; bytes 23-31 always 0; 0x73 diff = only phantom bit (offsets 67/68 = preamps 7/8) 0x00->0x10. macos-emumic-polar-patterns (2026-09-01, 247 OUT frames): each model 0..18 selected on preamps 7-8 and its polar-pattern control swept -- [22] observed at {0} for models 2/5/6/8/13/14/15/17, {0,1} for 1/12/16/18, {0,1,2} for 3/4/7, {0..8} for 9/10/11, {50} baseline for model 0. [21]/[23]/[24] always 0. One SET_LINK (0x14 a2 00 03 01) at t=6.5s = pair 3 (preamps 7&8) linked on enable. webui-emumic-preamp56-2026-09-03 (usbmon, webUI driving EMU on preamp 5/6): 14 e5 frames, [17]=05 constant, [18]=0x00 (preamp 5) and 0x01 (preamp 6) -- each change written to both -- [19] enable, [20] model (0x01/0x08/0x10 seen), [21] swap (0/1 both seen), [22] pattern (0/1 seen; model select preset it to the model default -- model 8 -> 0, model 16 -> 1). Disable emitted e5 [19]=0 (rest zeroed) then phantom-off (0x51 ch4/5) + gain re-sync (0x50 ch4/5) + unlink (0x14 a2 00 02 en 0). Confirms preamps 5-6 = link pair 2 and the channel_bias -4 mapping to [18]=0/1.","frame":"micmodeling_command (opcode 0x17 / param 0xe5) -- [18]=channel (0-based index - 4), [19]=enabled, [20]=model id, [21]=channel-order swap, [22]=polar pattern","model":"byte [20]. 0 = EdgeDuo / raw (no emulation, the default). 1..18 = the emulation models -- IDs + names + per-model pattern info in profiles/mic_models.json (captured for one account; may be list-position rather than global).","notes":"The 'emuMic' / mic-modeling feature -- Antelope's mic-emulation DSP, for their Edge Solo / Edge Duo / Edge Note modelling mics + model packs. Present on preamps 5-12 (the EMU button shows only when the channel is in Mic mode). emumic5 and emumic6 carry the same mono signal for a mono emulation (Edge Duo = 2 inputs collapsing to 1 modeled signal on both taps); a stereo modelling mic like the Edge Quadro (4 inputs) yields 2 distinct taps -- confirmed by listening test 2026-09-03, matches the Launcher. Decoded 2026-08-31: enable/pattern/swap from macos-ch7-8-micmodeling-* + macos-ch9-10_11-12-micmodeling-* (model 0, so [22] swept 0-100); model id [20] from emumic-model-select-... (Windows KVM, 18 models cycled on preamps 7-8); per-model polar-pattern index ranges from macos-emumic-polar-patterns (2026-09-01). Turning modeling ON auto-enables 48V phantom (param 0x51) and links the preamp pair (SET_LINK space 0); turning it OFF reverses all of it -- captured 2026-09-03 on preamps 5/6: e5 frame with [19]=0 (model/swap/pattern all zeroed), then SET_PARAM 0x51 ch4/ch5 value 0 (phantom off), then a SET_PARAM 0x50 ch4/ch5 gain re-sync (both channels stepped to the same values), then SET_LINK 0x14 a2 00 02 with enable 0 (unlink pair 2). No readback category identified (0x74/0x75 protocol; cat 0x1a is the surround EQ, cat 0x07 is unresolved -- neither covers mic modeling); in the passive stream only the phantom bit (0x10) shows. The client writes the e5 frame TWICE per change, once per channel of the pair ([18]=N then [18]=N+1, ~72 ms apart) -- same two-commands-per-pair pattern as the Launcher's link sync. build_micmodeling_command(profile, channel, enabled, pattern, swap, model); not in cli.py. MODEL SELECTION is account-bound -- Edge mics + model packs register to an Antelope account -- so the usable model list is per-user (profiles/mic_models.json).","pattern":"byte [22], a 0-based polar-pattern INDEX. With model 0: free 0-100 continuous morph -- 0 omni / 50 cardioid / 100 bi-directional (figure-8), every position valid (user-confirmed). With a selected emulation model: a small index into that model's pattern list, range per-model -- fixed mics lock at 0; 3-way mics (models 3,4,7) take 0/1/2; 9-detent multipattern mics (models 9,10,11) take 0..8; models 1,12,16,18 only 0..1 swept. Selecting a model presets [22] to the model's default index (0 / 1 / 4). Full per-model table in mic_models.json. (Corrected 2026-09-01 -- [22] was thought to carry a 'pattern_class' code for selected models; it does not, it is always the pattern index.)","per":"preamp channel (preamps 5-12; the EMU button shows only in Mic mode)","status":"confirmed -- enable / model / swap / pattern all decoded (2026-08-31); per-model polar-pattern index ranges added 2026-09-01; preamps 5-12 range FULLY CONFIRMED 2026-09-03 by a live webUI capture (0xe5 [18]=0x00 preamp 5 / 0x01 preamp 6, on the wire) + a listen test (emumic taps carry the modeled signal, model select audibly correct e.g. R112 model -> R112, emumic5==emumic6 mono for a mono emulation) -- matches the official Launcher. Nothing left open on the frame itself.","swap":"byte [21] -- a switch that swaps the channel order of the pair (user-confirmed)","type":"bool (enabled) + uint8 (model id) + bool (swap) + uint8 (pattern)"}

transport.notes: Confirmed from raw pcapng (2026-08): the vendor control protocol is entirely HID interrupt on interface 3, endpoint 0x01 OUT / 0x82 IN, device address 2 (usb.dst 1.2.x). Endpoints 0x05 OUT / 0x84 IN are the UAC2 isochronous audio stream (24-ch / 24-bit in the class-compliant descriptor) -- unrelated to control. Only 16 USB control transfers in the whole connect sequence: standard descriptor GETs + SET_CONFIGURATION/SET_INTERFACE, NO string-descriptor fetches in any capture on file. The UAC2 audio-control descriptor is a stub (1 clock source, 4 terminals all nrChannels=1, no Feature Units), so it carries no usable channel topology or names.
